subject: chemistry
title: Le Chatelier Loop: Stress and Response
welcome_lead: Predict how systems respond when concentration, pressure or T shifts.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on Le Chatelier's principle.
final_note: You can now nudge equilibria with precision.

concepts.def: System shifts to oppose imposed change.
Increase shifts to fewer gas moles.
At constant V no shift; constant P shifts.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Increasing pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas. Equal moles -> no shift.

Example: N2(g) + 3H2(g) <-> 2NH3(g) (4 mol -> 2 mol). High pressure pushes forward, raising NH3 yield (Haber process).

Only T changes Kc. Endothermic reaction: increasing T raises Kc. Exothermic: increases T lowers Kc.

For the Haber process (exothermic forward), high T lowers yield but raises rate -> compromise at ~400 deg C with Fe catalyst.

Catalysts lower activation energy for both directions equally. They reduce time to reach equilibrium but do not shift it.

Position and Kc are independent of catalyst presence.
